supplementary_table_02.basis: Author-written structural interpretation of the retained controller code, not an experimental measurement or automatic causal analysis.

rows.interpretation: A state-feedback oscillator drives the anterior joint, while the posterior joint follows with a phase lag. The Seed observes only joint state and has no target or flow input.
Bearing is converted into a signed, bounded steering command and distributed across the two joint accelerations without prescribing a world-frame route.
Body-frame forward and lateral velocity modify the bearing request, while large bearing error reserves actuator authority for redirection.
Joint phase redistributes steering toward the half-cycle already moving in the requested direction while preserving the travelling-wave carrier.
A transient burst augments the base asymmetry while large bearing error remains unmet. Recent bearing response, assisting yaw moment and high joint speed withdraw only this surplus authority.
Target-aligned relative crossflow replaces bearing history as the response signal used to release surplus redirect authority.
Lateral force must co-sign target-aligned crossflow before wake assistance releases the burst. This champion remained best through Iteration 20.
